function.name: look
function.description: Look around: every gatherable, world item, creature, player and station nearby, by its in-game name, with distance, what you can do with it and the id other tools act on. situation is only a short summary and misses many small things (sticks, stones, plants, chests): when he names something to pick up, use, fight or inspect that situation doesn't show, look with about=<his words> before acting on it or telling him it isn't there. Read-only: does not interrupt.

about.description: What the player named, in their words (e.g. 'sticks'). If nothing matches, the answer says matched=false and lists what IS around instead.

radius.description: Search radius in metres (the body caps it at 80).

max.description: At most this many entries, best matches first.

function.name: inspect
function.description: Details of one thing from a look result: what it is, what it gives, what it needs, which actions work. Read-only.

target.description: An id from a look result.

function.name: inventory
function.description: Your full inventory: what you wear (by slot), hold, carry on the hotbar (with durability) and in your bag, plus weight. Read-only: does not interrupt.

function.name: follow
function.description: Follow a player continuously until stopped or interrupted.

player.description: Name of the player to follow.

function.name: stop
function.description: Stop the current job (a follow too) and stand still and stay. Only for stopping or staying put: any other action already replaces the current job, so don't call stop beside one.

function.name: go_to
function.description: Walk to coordinates, a named place, a player or an entity.

target.description: A named place from notes, an entity id, a player name, or [x, y, z].

function.name: attack
function.description: Engage a target; reflexes keep fighting until it is resolved.

target.description: Entity id of the creature to attack, e.g. 'wolf_1'.

function.name: give
function.description: Hand carried items to a player (walks to them, drops at their feet). Players only: the game has no give to an NPC, an NPC takes what it wants in its conversation (talk).

function.name: pickup
function.description: Pick up an item lying on the ground into the companion's inventory.

target.description: World item id from state nearby_items, or 'nearest'.

item.description: Only items whose id or name contains this, e.g. 'oak'. ALWAYS set this when the player names what to pick up. Never pick up a different item than the one named: if nothing matching is in nearby_items, don't call pickup; say you can't see any.

limit.description: Pick up this many world items (nearest matching first).

function.name: drop
function.description: Drop carried items on the ground (at the companion's or Luis's feet).

item.description: Carried item: an id from state inventory, or a name like 'oak logs'.

at.description: At the companion's own feet, or at a nearby player's feet.

player.description: at=player: whose feet (the player must be close).

function.name: cast
function.description: Cast one of the spells in castable_spells now (self, an enemy id, or a point).

spell.description: Spell name as listed in castable_spells, e.g. 'Tempest Shield' or 'Windstep'.

target.description: Omit or 'self' for self spells; an entity id for a targeted spell; or [x, y, z].

walk_to.description: Only for cast_type instant_after_move: where to walk (id or [x, y, z]) while it is held open.

function.name: sleep
function.description: Go to sleep (nearest free bed, never someone else's) so the night can pass.

target.description: Omit for the nearest free bed; or a bed id.

mode.description: auto: a free bed if there is one, else summon a shelter and sleep in it.

function.name: wake
function.description: Get up after sleeping.

function.name: interact
function.description: Use a thing you looked at, like a player pressing E (gather sticks, open, pick).

target.description: An id from a look result whose actions include interact.

secondary.description: Use the thing's secondary interaction instead.

function.name: gather
function.description: Harvest a resource nearby until count is reached or it fails.

resource.description: Resource to harvest, e.g. 'oak' (oak logs), 'ash', 'stone' or 'rune_essence'.

count.description: How many more to gather (counted in the inventory).

radius.description: Initial search radius in metres (default 30; it widens when nothing is found).

function.name: set_reflex_rule
function.description: Store a standing order ('every time X, do Y') that your body runs by itself, instantly, during fights. It can only sense the triggers in trigger.kind: if his condition isn't one of them, don't call this, tell him you can't sense that. Same enemy + trigger replaces the old rule; reflex_rules lists the current ones. Does not interrupt your job.

kind.description: cast: cast a spell (spell, target self|enemy|cluster); evade: step away from the enemy (distance_m, default 4); switch_weapon: equip an owned weapon (item id); retreat: run back to Luis (duration_s, default 4); focus_target: switch the attack to the triggering enemy

target.description: cast: where to aim it.

item.description: switch_weapon: item id, e.g. 'ITEM_Club_Wood'.

duration_s.description: retreat: seconds to stay by Luis.

kind.description: What to react to. telegraph: an enemy of that kind starts an attack (raises claws, winds up); optional attack name filter; enemy_hp_below: the current target's health is below value percent; cluster_at_least: value or more enemies are bunched together around the target; own_hp_below: the companion's own health is below value percent; luis_hp_below: Luis's health is below value percent; enemy_stunned: the target is staggered or knocked down; spell_ready: the named spell is off cooldown and castable

value.description: Percent for *_hp_below, enemy count for cluster_at_least.

attack.description: telegraph only: part of the enemy attack name, if Luis named one.

near_m.description: telegraph only: how close the enemy must be (default 8 m).

enemy.description: Enemy kind it applies to, e.g. 'kalphite' (matches every Kalphite type), or '*' for any enemy. Rules are remembered per enemy kind.

actions.description: Done in order when it fires.

function.name: list_rules
function.description: List the standing orders (reflex rules).

enemy.description: Only rules that apply to this enemy kind.

function.name: clear_rule
function.description: Forget a standing order by id, every order for an enemy kind, or all.

enemy.description: Clear every rule for this enemy kind.

function.name: remember
function.description: Keep a fact for later (a place, a preference, something he told you); your notes show it in every request. For a place, use key 'place:<name>' with at=self (where you stand) or at=player (where that player stands), so its position is stored and go_to takes the name. Does not interrupt your job.

key.description: Short key, e.g. 'place:lake_hut' or 'pref:favourite_axe'; a 'state:<x>' note is a passing condition and is forgotten after 30 min.

at.description: For a place: store the position where you stand (self) or where a player stands (player).

player.description: With at=player: which player (default: the one talking).

function.name: run_skill
function.description: Run a skill you learned earlier with its params: learned_skills lists the ones that fit this request, with how often each worked. Prefer it to start_goal when one fits and its params are clear.

name.description: Name of a learned skill listed in learned_skills.

function.name: start_goal
function.description: Hand a long job of many steps to your planner (e.g. 'gather 10 logs and bring them to the player', 'build a storage hut by the lake'): it plans the steps with your tools, runs them, checks each in the game and reports back. A job one tool or a few calls in a row can do: call them yourself. A learned skill that fits: run_skill.

goal.description: The job in plain words, as he asked for it.

function.name: food_options
function.description: Read-only: your food or water options right now, each with what it restores, your level after, where it is, the steps, an estimated time and the risk. situation shows them by itself when a need is low.

function.name: agility_courses
function.description: Agility courses near you: name, distance, minimum level vs yours. Read only.

function.name: buildables
function.description: Pieces you can build (unlocked): name, category, material cost and what you're still missing. Read-only.

can_build_now.description: Only pieces you have the materials for.

about.description: Words for what to build; several things in one ask work (e.g. foundation wall roof door chest workbench). Each word gets its best pieces in the list, and by_word names them per word (a word with none has no piece).

function.name: combat_brief
function.description: Facts to prepare a fight: power levels, the creature's weaknesses, your weapons vs it, usable buff/defence spells, healing food, the estimate, its learned attacks. Read-only.

target.description: Creature id, or a name (nearest).

function.name: craft_plan
function.description: Plan a goal item from carried items: ordered steps (gather, craft at station, unlock, find station) and alternative recipes. Read only.

quantity_mode.description: additional_output: make count more; inventory_target: end up carrying count in total.

item.description: Goal item name or id.

function.name: farm_plots
function.description: Farm plots near you with the game's own state: soil (weeds/clear), harvestable, diseased, watered, fertilized, the plot's prompt, growth (what grows there and its stage, e.g. Potato stage 2 of 3, from the plant the game shows; weeds count as a plant) and mine (true: a plot I built; false: someone else's). Read only.

function.name: fishing_spots
function.description: Fishing spots near you: method (net/rod), level, distance, fished out or not, and which of your tools fits each. Read only.

function.name: held_actions
function.description: The actions of what you hold, from item data: style, name (e.g. Chop, Overhead Chop), perk, unlocked, damage. Read-only.

function.name: inspect
function.description: Details of one thing: what it gives, needs, contains. Read-only.

target.description: An id from look.

function.name: inventory
function.description: Your full inventory with item stats vs what you wear. Read-only.

function.name: lodestones
function.description: Lodestones you could fast-travel to: where they are, whether teleport is currently available from the nearest one, and the cost. Read-only.

function.name: look
function.description: List things nearby (items, plants, resources, creatures, players, usables) with the ids other tools act on. situation is only a short summary and misses many small things (sticks, stones, plants, chests, stations): when he names something to pick up, use, fight or inspect that situation doesn't show, look with about=<his words> before acting on it or telling him it isn't there. Read-only.

near.description: A player's name: look around HIM instead of you (distances from him, plus from_me and which side of him it lies). He must be in sight.

about.description: The player's words for what to find; ranks matches first.

function.name: quests
function.description: Your quest log from the game: active quests with the current step in the game's own words (and its hint), and where: the step's own map markers as the map and compass show them (an area circle, a target spot or the NPC: name, kind, radius_m, position, distance_m, inside); go_to takes the position. Completed quests too; all = true adds the ones not started. Read only.

function.name: recipes
function.description: List recipes: craftable now (default), every recipe for an item with its status and missing inputs, or what a station makes. Read-only.

item.description: Item name or id.

function.name: spells
function.description: Your spells: what each does, rune cost vs carried, cooldown, castable now and why not. all=true adds locked ones with their unlock level. Read-only.

function.name: stations
function.description: Stations near you: type, distance, unlocked recipes, what you can make now, and a furnace's state (running, contents, fuel, output). Read-only.

function.name: agility_course
function.description: Run an agility course: walks to its start, starts it, and runs through its orbs to the finish. Trains Agility (walking anywhere also gives a little Agility XP). See agility_courses.

course.description: A course id from agility_courses (default: the nearest you can do).

function.name: attack
function.description: Fight a creature until it dies, defending per combat_orders (never players). data.assessment estimates the fight. The kill trains the skill of the weapon you hold (melee: Attack, bows: Ranged, staffs: Magic; `weapon` picks it, default best melee).

style.description: A held item's action: primary, special, secondary, jump, or its name (held_actions).

weapon.description: Carried item to fight with (e.g. a crossbow), or held = what is in hand now; default best melee.

target.description: Creature id, or a name (nearest).

function.name: build
function.description: Build a piece by its name from buildables (you need its materials), or several with pieces. Walks near the spot (stays put when it is in reach), tries preview spots until one is valid, places it once and checks it was built. ok: 'built' says what stands where (metres and compass from you, facing, its structures id); rejected_previews_before_placing are not failures. With on, it only places once the preview snaps onto that piece and says whether it sits flush (gap, level, facing). Not ok: detail says why, and no new piece was found standing there. Trains Construction.

near.description: Somewhere next to this id: 'me' is beside you wherever this step finds you (a gather or walk before it may have taken you away from your house); a built piece's id (your house's foundation) puts it by that piece.

piece.description: The piece's name or id from buildables (words of its name are enough when only one piece has them all).

rotation.description: Turn it this many degrees (15 degree steps).

pieces.description: Several in one go, the build screen kept open: a list of {piece, on, rotation}. on may name an earlier item as '#k' ('#1:N' = the N edge of what item 1 built). I go in the order that keeps walking short;

on.description: Attach to a built piece: its structures id, optionally ':N', ':E', ':S', ':W', ':top' or ':in' (no side: the free side nearest you). What holds what: a wall or door-frame wall stands on a foundation's edge (':N' = its north edge); ':in' puts a door into a door-frame wall;

at.description: Exactly here: [x, y, z] metres or an id.

function.name: cast
function.description: Cast one of your spells (wheel, then cast); verified by runes and cooldown. Pick from castable_spells by what it does; a spell not listed there can't be cast now, so tell him so instead. Instant: on you. Placed/aimed: at target, or omit it and you find a valid spot or aim yourself; a target out of reach (even a moving creature) is walked up to and cast at in this same call. Each spell's `how` (in castable_spells) says how it is really used: what to drop or stand by first, what to cast it on, or (cast_type instant_after_move) that it is held open while you walk_to somewhere. Never at players.

target.description: Placed/aimed: look id or [x,y,z] m; omit to choose.

walk_to.description: Required for, and only for, cast_type instant_after_move: walk here (look id or [x,y,z] m) while it is held open, then finish it; the result says where you ended (landed_at), how far from where you opened it (from_opened_m) and whether that brought you back (returned).

function.name: collect_water
function.description: Collect water (Dirty Water) from a pond or river: walks to the bank, uses the water, checks it came in; repeats for count. Dirty Water is drinkable but unhealthy; boil it at a Campfire for Clean Water.

target.description: A water source's id from look (default: the nearest water).

function.name: combat_orders
function.description: Set your standing combat policy, kept until changed.

disengage.description: Back off and eat when hurt.

abilities.description: Spells the reflex may use: {phase_dash, windstep, tempest_shield} true/false.

function.name: consume
function.description: Eat or drink one item you carry (a bag item is dragged to your hotbar and used; ground items: interact first). Food and drink each have their own use lock (~6 s): a drink right after a food goes at once, a second food waits ~6 s for the first.

item.description: A carried item's name or id, or 'food' / 'drink' / 'potion'.

function.name: craft
function.description: Make one recipe at a nearby station from carried items (walks there, uses it, collects the result). It needs every input carried, the recipe unlocked and a station of its type: without one it fails and says which. What a recipe takes, and what of it you are short of, is read with recipes. It does not gather or craft ingredients (craft_plan plans those).

item.description: Item to make (name or id).

recipe.description: Recipe id, to pick one of several.

input.description: Or a carried item to put in the station instead of naming what comes out (e.g. raw food at a fire): the recipe that takes it.

count.description: Items, default 1 (crafts with recipe or input; input without count: all of it).

function.name: deconstruct
function.description: Take down a built piece the way a player does (build menu, repair mode, aim, destroy), or with whole=true every piece connected to it, top first so nothing falls. Says what came down, what you got back (the materials it cost: they drop beside it and I walk over them; any still on the ground are named with their ids in on_ground, for fetch) and what was left and why. Never takes a container that holds items; stations, farm plots and containers that aren't yours stay unless the player asked for that one (include_stations); a piece something kept stands on stays.

include_stations.description: Also an empty station / plot / container that isn't yours, only when the player asked for it.

whole.description: Also every piece connected to it (the whole house).

target.description: A structures id (get_state / look), e.g. BuildingPiece_42 or an actor id.

function.name: drop
function.description: Drop carried items at your feet (to hand them to a player use give).

item.description: A carried item: its name (e.g. 'Oak Logs') or item id from inventory.

function.name: equip
function.description: Equip a carried weapon, tool, shield or armour piece; answers once the game shows it in your hands or worn.

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

function.name: explore
function.description: Search outward on foot with no place in mind, least-visited directions first, until something matching 'about' comes into view; reports what was found or how far you searched. It does not head for a place you know of (a quest's marker, a named or remembered place): go_to goes there.

about.description: What to look for, in words (e.g. water, berries, a tree).

function.name: fish
function.description: Fish at a fishing spot (ripples in the water) until you catch count more: walks there, takes out the net or rod that spot needs, trawls (net) or casts and fights the fish (rod). Trains Fishing. Needs a carried net or rod that fits the spot (see fishing_spots).

method.description: Only spots of this method, e.g. net or rod (from fishing_spots).

spot.description: A fishing spot id from fishing_spots (default: the nearest one you have a tool for).

function.name: follow
function.description: Follow a player until stopped or given another job (waits and resumes if he is out of reach; out of sight, goes by his marker on the game map).

function.name: gather
function.description: Harvest a resource (a profile key, e.g. oak, ash, copper, stone_boulder, loose_stones) until you have count MORE; finds targets and equips your tool. The result's `trains` names the skill it gave XP to (none = no XP). Trains Mining: clay, coal, copper, iron, rune_essence, stone_boulder, tin; Trains Woodcutting: ash, maple, oak, willow, yew; no XP: loose_stones (other profiles: not measured).

mode.description: Only sources of this kind (chop, pickup); no tool-free substitute.

style.description: One of the tool's actions (see held_actions), e.g. Overhead Chop.

target.description: The id of one log or stump lying here (from what you see) to chop up and collect; ends when it and its pieces are done.

resource.description: A resource (oak, copper, stone_boulder = mine a stone boulder with a pickaxe, Mining XP; loose_stones = pick stones up off the ground, no XP) or a kind (ore, rock, logs, stone: the nearest of that kind).

near.description: A player's name: search around HIM instead of you (he must be in sight).

function.name: give
function.description: Hand carried items to a player the way players do (the game has no trade): walk to him (any distance), step in front of him, face him, drop the count at his feet and check it lies there. He picks it up himself. Players only: an NPC takes what a quest asks for in the talk with them (talk).

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

function.name: go_to
function.description: Walk to a player, a perceived thing, a remembered place or a point; answers on arrival or says why not. Use it whenever he wants you somewhere, also when you think you're already there: it answers arrived at once if you are. A player out of sight is found by his marker on the game map, at any distance.

target.description: A player name, a perceived id, a place, 'my_grave' / 'my_grave:<ts>' (a remembered grave), or [x,y,z]. Also a place name from the game's map (a region, NPC or landmark), even out of sight, or a lodestone by what stands near it ("the lodestone by Zanik"): pass the name itself, no need to look for it…

function.name: interact
function.description: Press use (E) on one perceived thing: walks there, faces it, presses, checks it worked. Picks up a ground stack or plant, Take All from a grave, lies down in a bed/shelter (interact on it again to get up), opens, talks. To only walk to something, use go_to.

secondary.description: Its second action (F), e.g. collect every nearby stack of that kind.

target.description: The id of one perceived thing (from situation or look). Not a name or coordinates.

function.name: move_item
function.description: Move a carried item between bag and hotbar (only hotbar food/drink can be used).

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

slot.description: Slot in that page (default: first free).

function.name: set_vitals_policy
function.description: Set when your reflex eats, drinks or eats to heal by itself (% of max; a 10% floor always applies).

reserve_warn.description: Warn below this many usable items.

heal_below_pct.description: Eat healing food below this % HP (0 = off).

function.name: split
function.description: Split a carried stack in two: take count off it into a free slot, the rest stays (e.g. to drop, store or give only part). drop, store and give take the amount themselves, so split only when a separate stack is wanted.

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

to.description: Where the new stack goes (default: beside the old one).

count.description: How many go into the new stack.

function.name: stop
function.description: Stop the current job (a follow too) and stand still and stay. Only for stopping or staying put: any other action already replaces the current job, so don't call stop beside one.

function.name: store
function.description: Put carried items into a chest or storage: walks there, opens it, moves them in, checks, closes it.

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

container.description: The chest's id (from situation or look).

function.name: take
function.description: Take items out of a chest or storage: walks there, opens it, moves them to your bag or hotbar, checks, closes it. Shared chests are fine; say what you took.

item.description: The item's name or id.

container.description: The chest's id (from situation or look).

function.name: talk
function.description: Talk to someone (an NPC whose prompt is Talk): walks over, opens the conversation and returns everything they say and your numbered answer options, exactly as the game shows them. Answer in the next call with choose = the option's number or text, or end it with leave = true; call with no arguments to re-read. Each reply reports quest steps that changed (quests_changed) and items they gave or took (items). Quest hand-ins happen by talking to the quest's NPC while you carry or have done what the step asks.

choose.description: Your answer: an option number or its text, from the last reply.

target.description: Who to talk to: their name (e.g. from look or the quest step) or an id from look (only to start).

function.name: teleport
function.description: Fast-travel like a player to a far lodestone (another region): walk to the nearest lodestone, use it, pick the destination on its map; checks you arrived. Not for getting to a lodestone: walking to one, also one he names by what stands near it ('the lodestone by Zanik'), is go_to.

to.description: A lodestone id from lodestones, or [x, y, z] metres (the lodestone nearest that point).

function.name: tend
function.description: Work a farm plot once: walk to it and use a carried item on it (its main action, e.g. a spade's dig, seeds' scatter, a watering can's pour, compost), or with no item press use on it (harvest, cure). Checks the plot changed. A spade on a weeded plot keeps digging until the soil is clear (the game needs about 5 digs per weed stage). Trains Farming. See farm_plots for each plot's state.

times.description: Presses at most, until the plot changes.

item.description: A carried item to use on the plot (name or id); omit to press use.

plot.description: A plot id from farm_plots (default: the nearest).

function.name: unequip
function.description: Put away a held item or take off a worn piece (into your bag); answers once the game shows it off.

slot.description: Or a loadout slot: HeldRight, HeldLeft, Head, Body, Legs, Cape.

item.description: The equipped item's name or id.

function.name: use_action
function.description: Use one of your held item's actions once (a swing, a block, the special), e.g. to show the player.

style.description: A held item's action: primary, special, secondary, jump, or its name (held_actions).

function.name: lookup
function.description: Look up game knowledge: what an item is and does, how to make it, which regions of the world something is found in, creatures and weaknesses, spells, perks, mechanics, and a quest's walkthrough (look up the quest's name: its steps as players do them, what to bring, where to go). Game data first (authoritative), then the wiki with page links. Use it for a game fact you're not sure of instead of guessing, and when a quest step is new to you or doesn't say how to do it. Read-only: does not interrupt. kind values: item, recipe, station, location.

query.description: The thing or topic, in a few words: an item, recipe, creature, place, spell, perk, station or mechanic (e.g. 'pumpkin spice infusion', 'iron bar', 'oak tree', 'over eating').

kind.description: Optional filter, e.g. item, recipe, station, spell, perk, monster, resource node, location. Ignored when nothing of that kind matches.

function.name: remember
function.description: Keep a fact for later (a place, a preference, something he told you); your notes show it in every request. For a place, use key 'place:<name>' with at=self (where you stand) or at=player (where that player stands), so its position is stored and go_to takes the name. Does not interrupt your job.

key.description: Short key, e.g. 'place:lake_hut' or 'pref:favourite_axe'; a 'state:<x>' note is a passing condition and is forgotten after 30 min.

at.description: For a place: store the position where you stand (self) or where a player stands (player).

player.description: With at=player: which player (default: the one talking).

function.name: run_skill
function.description: Run a skill you learned earlier with its params: learned_skills lists the ones that fit this request, with how often each worked. Prefer it to start_goal when one fits and its params are clear.

name.description: Name of a learned skill listed in learned_skills.

function.name: start_goal
function.description: Hand a long job of many steps to your planner (e.g. 'gather 10 logs and bring them to the player', 'build a storage hut by the lake'): it plans the steps with your tools, runs them, checks each in the game and reports back. A job one tool or a few calls in a row can do: call them yourself. A learned skill that fits: run_skill.

goal.description: The job in plain words, as he asked for it.

function.name: list_skills
function.description: Read-only: the skills you have learned, with how often each worked.

function.name: forget_skill
function.description: Delete one learned skill by its exact name (from list_skills).

function.name: food_options
function.description: Read-only: your food or water options right now, each with what it restores, your level after, where it is, the steps, an estimated time and the risk. situation shows them by itself when a need is low.

function.name: agility_courses
function.description: Agility courses near you: name, distance, minimum level vs yours. Read only.

function.name: buildables
function.description: Pieces you can build (unlocked): name, category, material cost and what you're still missing. Read-only.

can_build_now.description: Only pieces you have the materials for.

about.description: Words for what to build; several things in one ask work (e.g. foundation wall roof door chest workbench). Each word gets its best pieces in the list, and by_word names them per word (a word with none has no piece).

function.name: combat_brief
function.description: Facts to prepare a fight: power levels, the creature's weaknesses, your weapons vs it, usable buff/defence spells, healing food, the estimate, its learned attacks. Read-only.

target.description: Creature id, or a name (nearest).

function.name: craft_plan
function.description: Plan a goal item from carried items: ordered steps (gather, craft at station, unlock, find station) and alternative recipes. Read only.

quantity_mode.description: additional_output: make count more; inventory_target: end up carrying count in total.

item.description: Goal item name or id.

function.name: farm_plots
function.description: Farm plots near you with the game's own state: soil (weeds/clear), harvestable, diseased, watered, fertilized, the plot's prompt, growth (what grows there and its stage, e.g. Potato stage 2 of 3, from the plant the game shows; weeds count as a plant) and mine (true: a plot I built; false: someone else's). Read only.

function.name: fishing_spots
function.description: Fishing spots near you: method (net/rod), level, distance, fished out or not, and which of your tools fits each. Read only.

function.name: held_actions
function.description: The actions of what you hold, from item data: style, name (e.g. Chop, Overhead Chop), perk, unlocked, damage. Read-only.

function.name: inspect
function.description: Details of one thing: what it gives, needs, contains. Read-only.

target.description: An id from look.

function.name: inventory
function.description: Your full inventory with item stats vs what you wear. Read-only.

function.name: lodestones
function.description: Lodestones you could fast-travel to: where they are, whether teleport is currently available from the nearest one, and the cost. Read-only.

function.name: look
function.description: List things nearby (items, plants, resources, creatures, players, usables) with the ids other tools act on. situation is only a short summary and misses many small things (sticks, stones, plants, chests, stations): when he names something to pick up, use, fight or inspect that situation doesn't show, look with about=<his words> before acting on it or telling him it isn't there. Read-only.

near.description: A player's name: look around HIM instead of you (distances from him, plus from_me and which side of him it lies). He must be in sight.

about.description: The player's words for what to find; ranks matches first.

function.name: quests
function.description: Your quest log from the game: active quests with the current step in the game's own words (and its hint), and where: the step's own map markers as the map and compass show them (an area circle, a target spot or the NPC: name, kind, radius_m, position, distance_m, inside); go_to takes the position. Completed quests too; all = true adds the ones not started. Read only.

function.name: recipes
function.description: List recipes: craftable now (default), every recipe for an item with its status and missing inputs, or what a station makes. Read-only.

item.description: Item name or id.

function.name: spells
function.description: Your spells: what each does, rune cost vs carried, cooldown, castable now and why not. all=true adds locked ones with their unlock level. Read-only.

function.name: stations
function.description: Stations near you: type, distance, unlocked recipes, what you can make now, and a furnace's state (running, contents, fuel, output). Read-only.

function.name: agility_course
function.description: Run an agility course: walks to its start, starts it, and runs through its orbs to the finish. Trains Agility (walking anywhere also gives a little Agility XP). See agility_courses.

course.description: A course id from agility_courses (default: the nearest you can do).

function.name: attack
function.description: Fight a creature until it dies, defending per combat_orders (never players). data.assessment estimates the fight. The kill trains the skill of the weapon you hold (melee: Attack, bows: Ranged, staffs: Magic; `weapon` picks it, default best melee).

style.description: A held item's action: primary, special, secondary, jump, or its name (held_actions).

weapon.description: Carried item to fight with (e.g. a crossbow), or held = what is in hand now; default best melee.

target.description: Creature id, or a name (nearest).

function.name: build
function.description: Build a piece by its name from buildables (you need its materials), or several with pieces. Walks near the spot (stays put when it is in reach), tries preview spots until one is valid, places it once and checks it was built. ok: 'built' says what stands where (metres and compass from you, facing, its structures id); rejected_previews_before_placing are not failures. With on, it only places once the preview snaps onto that piece and says whether it sits flush (gap, level, facing). Not ok: detail says why, and no new piece was found standing there. Trains Construction.

near.description: Somewhere next to this id: 'me' is beside you wherever this step finds you (a gather or walk before it may have taken you away from your house); a built piece's id (your house's foundation) puts it by that piece.

piece.description: The piece's name or id from buildables (words of its name are enough when only one piece has them all).

rotation.description: Turn it this many degrees (15 degree steps).

pieces.description: Several in one go, the build screen kept open: a list of {piece, on, rotation}. on may name an earlier item as '#k' ('#1:N' = the N edge of what item 1 built). I go in the order that keeps walking short;

on.description: Attach to a built piece: its structures id, optionally ':N', ':E', ':S', ':W', ':top' or ':in' (no side: the free side nearest you). What holds what: a wall or door-frame wall stands on a foundation's edge (':N' = its north edge); ':in' puts a door into a door-frame wall;

at.description: Exactly here: [x, y, z] metres or an id.

function.name: cast
function.description: Cast one of your spells (wheel, then cast); verified by runes and cooldown. Pick from castable_spells by what it does; a spell not listed there can't be cast now, so tell him so instead. Instant: on you. Placed/aimed: at target, or omit it and you find a valid spot or aim yourself; a target out of reach (even a moving creature) is walked up to and cast at in this same call. Each spell's `how` (in castable_spells) says how it is really used: what to drop or stand by first, what to cast it on, or (cast_type instant_after_move) that it is held open while you walk_to somewhere. Never at players.

target.description: Placed/aimed: look id or [x,y,z] m; omit to choose.

walk_to.description: Required for, and only for, cast_type instant_after_move: walk here (look id or [x,y,z] m) while it is held open, then finish it; the result says where you ended (landed_at), how far from where you opened it (from_opened_m) and whether that brought you back (returned).

function.name: collect_water
function.description: Collect water (Dirty Water) from a pond or river: walks to the bank, uses the water, checks it came in; repeats for count. Dirty Water is drinkable but unhealthy; boil it at a Campfire for Clean Water.

target.description: A water source's id from look (default: the nearest water).

function.name: combat_orders
function.description: Set your standing combat policy, kept until changed.

disengage.description: Back off and eat when hurt.

abilities.description: Spells the reflex may use: {phase_dash, windstep, tempest_shield} true/false.

function.name: consume
function.description: Eat or drink one item you carry (a bag item is dragged to your hotbar and used; ground items: interact first). Food and drink each have their own use lock (~6 s): a drink right after a food goes at once, a second food waits ~6 s for the first.

item.description: A carried item's name or id, or 'food' / 'drink' / 'potion'.

function.name: craft
function.description: Make one recipe at a nearby station from carried items (walks there, uses it, collects the result). It needs every input carried, the recipe unlocked and a station of its type: without one it fails and says which. What a recipe takes, and what of it you are short of, is read with recipes. It does not gather or craft ingredients (craft_plan plans those).

item.description: Item to make (name or id).

recipe.description: Recipe id, to pick one of several.

input.description: Or a carried item to put in the station instead of naming what comes out (e.g. raw food at a fire): the recipe that takes it.

count.description: Items, default 1 (crafts with recipe or input; input without count: all of it).

function.name: deconstruct
function.description: Take down a built piece the way a player does (build menu, repair mode, aim, destroy), or with whole=true every piece connected to it, top first so nothing falls. Says what came down, what you got back (the materials it cost: they drop beside it and I walk over them; any still on the ground are named with their ids in on_ground, for fetch) and what was left and why. Never takes a container that holds items; stations, farm plots and containers that aren't yours stay unless the player asked for that one (include_stations); a piece something kept stands on stays.

include_stations.description: Also an empty station / plot / container that isn't yours, only when the player asked for it.

whole.description: Also every piece connected to it (the whole house).

target.description: A structures id (get_state / look), e.g. BuildingPiece_42 or an actor id.

function.name: drop
function.description: Drop carried items at your feet (to hand them to a player use give).

item.description: A carried item: its name (e.g. 'Oak Logs') or item id from inventory.

function.name: equip
function.description: Equip a carried weapon, tool, shield or armour piece; answers once the game shows it in your hands or worn.

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

function.name: explore
function.description: Search outward on foot with no place in mind, least-visited directions first, until something matching 'about' comes into view; reports what was found or how far you searched. It does not head for a place you know of (a quest's marker, a named or remembered place): go_to goes there.

about.description: What to look for, in words (e.g. water, berries, a tree).

function.name: fish
function.description: Fish at a fishing spot (ripples in the water) until you catch count more: walks there, takes out the net or rod that spot needs, trawls (net) or casts and fights the fish (rod). Trains Fishing. Needs a carried net or rod that fits the spot (see fishing_spots).

method.description: Only spots of this method, e.g. net or rod (from fishing_spots).

spot.description: A fishing spot id from fishing_spots (default: the nearest one you have a tool for).

function.name: follow
function.description: Follow a player until stopped or given another job (waits and resumes if he is out of reach; out of sight, goes by his marker on the game map).

function.name: gather
function.description: Harvest a resource (a profile key, e.g. oak, ash, copper, stone_boulder, loose_stones) until you have count MORE; finds targets and equips your tool. The result's `trains` names the skill it gave XP to (none = no XP). Trains Mining: clay, coal, copper, iron, rune_essence, stone_boulder, tin; Trains Woodcutting: ash, maple, oak, willow, yew; no XP: loose_stones (other profiles: not measured).

mode.description: Only sources of this kind (chop, pickup); no tool-free substitute.

style.description: One of the tool's actions (see held_actions), e.g. Overhead Chop.

target.description: The id of one log or stump lying here (from what you see) to chop up and collect; ends when it and its pieces are done.

resource.description: A resource (oak, copper, stone_boulder = mine a stone boulder with a pickaxe, Mining XP; loose_stones = pick stones up off the ground, no XP) or a kind (ore, rock, logs, stone: the nearest of that kind).

near.description: A player's name: search around HIM instead of you (he must be in sight).

function.name: give
function.description: Hand carried items to a player the way players do (the game has no trade): walk to him (any distance), step in front of him, face him, drop the count at his feet and check it lies there. He picks it up himself. Players only: an NPC takes what a quest asks for in the talk with them (talk).

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

function.name: go_to
function.description: Walk to a player, a perceived thing, a remembered place or a point; answers on arrival or says why not. Use it whenever he wants you somewhere, also when you think you're already there: it answers arrived at once if you are. A player out of sight is found by his marker on the game map, at any distance.

target.description: A player name, a perceived id, a place, 'my_grave' / 'my_grave:<ts>' (a remembered grave), or [x,y,z]. Also a place name from the game's map (a region, NPC or landmark), even out of sight, or a lodestone by what stands near it ("the lodestone by Zanik"): pass the name itself, no need to look for it…

function.name: interact
function.description: Press use (E) on one perceived thing: walks there, faces it, presses, checks it worked. Picks up a ground stack or plant, Take All from a grave, lies down in a bed/shelter (interact on it again to get up), opens, talks. To only walk to something, use go_to.

secondary.description: Its second action (F), e.g. collect every nearby stack of that kind.

target.description: The id of one perceived thing (from situation or look). Not a name or coordinates.

function.name: move_item
function.description: Move a carried item between bag and hotbar (only hotbar food/drink can be used).

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

slot.description: Slot in that page (default: first free).

function.name: set_vitals_policy
function.description: Set when your reflex eats, drinks or eats to heal by itself (% of max; a 10% floor always applies).

reserve_warn.description: Warn below this many usable items.

heal_below_pct.description: Eat healing food below this % HP (0 = off).

function.name: split
function.description: Split a carried stack in two: take count off it into a free slot, the rest stays (e.g. to drop, store or give only part). drop, store and give take the amount themselves, so split only when a separate stack is wanted.

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

to.description: Where the new stack goes (default: beside the old one).

count.description: How many go into the new stack.

function.name: stop
function.description: Stop the current job (a follow too) and stand still and stay. Only for stopping or staying put: any other action already replaces the current job, so don't call stop beside one.

function.name: store
function.description: Put carried items into a chest or storage: walks there, opens it, moves them in, checks, closes it.

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

container.description: The chest's id (from situation or look).

function.name: take
function.description: Take items out of a chest or storage: walks there, opens it, moves them to your bag or hotbar, checks, closes it. Shared chests are fine; say what you took.

item.description: The item's name or id.

container.description: The chest's id (from situation or look).

function.name: talk
function.description: Talk to someone (an NPC whose prompt is Talk): walks over, opens the conversation and returns everything they say and your numbered answer options, exactly as the game shows them. Answer in the next call with choose = the option's number or text, or end it with leave = true; call with no arguments to re-read. Each reply reports quest steps that changed (quests_changed) and items they gave or took (items). Quest hand-ins happen by talking to the quest's NPC while you carry or have done what the step asks.

choose.description: Your answer: an option number or its text, from the last reply.

target.description: Who to talk to: their name (e.g. from look or the quest step) or an id from look (only to start).

function.name: teleport
function.description: Fast-travel like a player to a far lodestone (another region): walk to the nearest lodestone, use it, pick the destination on its map; checks you arrived. Not for getting to a lodestone: walking to one, also one he names by what stands near it ('the lodestone by Zanik'), is go_to.

to.description: A lodestone id from lodestones, or [x, y, z] metres (the lodestone nearest that point).

function.name: tend
function.description: Work a farm plot once: walk to it and use a carried item on it (its main action, e.g. a spade's dig, seeds' scatter, a watering can's pour, compost), or with no item press use on it (harvest, cure). Checks the plot changed. A spade on a weeded plot keeps digging until the soil is clear (the game needs about 5 digs per weed stage). Trains Farming. See farm_plots for each plot's state.

times.description: Presses at most, until the plot changes.

item.description: A carried item to use on the plot (name or id); omit to press use.

plot.description: A plot id from farm_plots (default: the nearest).

function.name: unequip
function.description: Put away a held item or take off a worn piece (into your bag); answers once the game shows it off.

slot.description: Or a loadout slot: HeldRight, HeldLeft, Head, Body, Legs, Cape.

item.description: The equipped item's name or id.

function.name: use_action
function.description: Use one of your held item's actions once (a swing, a block, the special), e.g. to show the player.

style.description: A held item's action: primary, special, secondary, jump, or its name (held_actions).

function.name: lookup
function.description: Look up game knowledge: what an item is and does, how to make it, which regions of the world something is found in, creatures and weaknesses, spells, perks, mechanics, and a quest's walkthrough (look up the quest's name: its steps as players do them, what to bring, where to go). Game data first (authoritative), then the wiki with page links. Use it for a game fact you're not sure of instead of guessing, and when a quest step is new to you or doesn't say how to do it. Read-only: does not interrupt. kind values: item, recipe, station, location.

query.description: The thing or topic, in a few words: an item, recipe, creature, place, spell, perk, station or mechanic (e.g. 'pumpkin spice infusion', 'iron bar', 'oak tree', 'over eating').

kind.description: Optional filter, e.g. item, recipe, station, spell, perk, monster, resource node, location. Ignored when nothing of that kind matches.

function.name: remember
function.description: Keep a fact for later (a place, a preference, something he told you); your notes show it in every request. For a place, use key 'place:<name>' with at=self (where you stand) or at=player (where that player stands), so its position is stored and go_to takes the name. Does not interrupt your job.

key.description: Short key, e.g. 'place:lake_hut' or 'pref:favourite_axe'; a 'state:<x>' note is a passing condition and is forgotten after 30 min.

at.description: For a place: store the position where you stand (self) or where a player stands (player).

player.description: With at=player: which player (default: the one talking).

function.name: run_skill
function.description: Run a skill you learned earlier with its params: learned_skills lists the ones that fit this request, with how often each worked. Prefer it to start_goal when one fits and its params are clear.

name.description: Name of a learned skill listed in learned_skills.

function.name: list_skills
function.description: Read-only: the skills you have learned, with how often each worked.

function.name: forget_skill
function.description: Delete one learned skill by its exact name (from list_skills).

function.name: food_options
function.description: Read-only: your food or water options right now, each with what it restores, your level after, where it is, the steps, an estimated time and the risk. situation shows them by itself when a need is low.

function.name: board
function.description: The task board. Read-only.

function.name: add_task
function.description: Add a job.

function.name: say
function.description: Say one line in game chat. This is the only way anyone hears you: text you write outside say is a private note nobody sees. Call it at most once per reply, beside your other tool calls; the line is said when they start (if one fails first, you get to say what went wrong instead). No say call = you stay silent.

text.description: Exactly what the players read in chat: short, casual, in your own words.

function.name: look
function.description: Look around: every gatherable, world item, creature, player and station nearby, by its in-game name, with distance, what you can do with it and the id other tools act on. situation is only a short summary and misses many small things (sticks, stones, plants, chests): when he names something to pick up, use, fight or inspect that situation doesn't show, look with about=<his words> before acting on it or telling him it isn't there. Read-only: does not interrupt.

about.description: What the player named, in their words (e.g. 'sticks'). If nothing matches, the answer says matched=false and lists what IS around instead.

radius.description: Search radius in metres (the body caps it at 80).

max.description: At most this many entries, best matches first.

function.name: inspect
function.description: Details of one thing from a look result: what it is, what it gives, what it needs, which actions work. Read-only.

target.description: An id from a look result.

function.name: inventory
function.description: Your full inventory: what you wear (by slot), hold, carry on the hotbar (with durability) and in your bag, plus weight. Read-only: does not interrupt.

function.name: follow
function.description: Follow a player continuously until stopped or interrupted.

player.description: Name of the player to follow.

function.name: stop
function.description: Stop the current job (a follow too) and stand still and stay. Only for stopping or staying put: any other action already replaces the current job, so don't call stop beside one.

function.name: go_to
function.description: Walk to coordinates, a named place, a player or an entity.

target.description: A named place from notes, an entity id, a player name, or [x, y, z].

function.name: attack
function.description: Engage a target; reflexes keep fighting until it is resolved.

target.description: Entity id of the creature to attack, e.g. 'wolf_1'.

function.name: give
function.description: Hand carried items to a player (walks to them, drops at their feet). Players only: the game has no give to an NPC, an NPC takes what it wants in its conversation (talk).

function.name: pickup
function.description: Pick up an item lying on the ground into the companion's inventory.

target.description: World item id from state nearby_items, or 'nearest'.

item.description: Only items whose id or name contains this, e.g. 'oak'. ALWAYS set this when the player names what to pick up. Never pick up a different item than the one named: if nothing matching is in nearby_items, don't call pickup; say you can't see any.

limit.description: Pick up this many world items (nearest matching first).

function.name: drop
function.description: Drop carried items on the ground (at the companion's or Luis's feet).

item.description: Carried item: an id from state inventory, or a name like 'oak logs'.

at.description: At the companion's own feet, or at a nearby player's feet.

player.description: at=player: whose feet (the player must be close).

function.name: cast
function.description: Cast one of the spells in castable_spells now (self, an enemy id, or a point).

spell.description: Spell name as listed in castable_spells, e.g. 'Tempest Shield' or 'Windstep'.

target.description: Omit or 'self' for self spells; an entity id for a targeted spell; or [x, y, z].

walk_to.description: Only for cast_type instant_after_move: where to walk (id or [x, y, z]) while it is held open.

function.name: sleep
function.description: Go to sleep (nearest free bed, never someone else's) so the night can pass.

target.description: Omit for the nearest free bed; or a bed id.

mode.description: auto: a free bed if there is one, else summon a shelter and sleep in it.

function.name: wake
function.description: Get up after sleeping.

function.name: interact
function.description: Use a thing you looked at, like a player pressing E (gather sticks, open, pick).

target.description: An id from a look result whose actions include interact.

secondary.description: Use the thing's secondary interaction instead.

function.name: gather
function.description: Harvest a resource nearby until count is reached or it fails.

resource.description: Resource to harvest, e.g. 'oak' (oak logs), 'ash', 'stone' or 'rune_essence'.

count.description: How many more to gather (counted in the inventory).

radius.description: Initial search radius in metres (default 30; it widens when nothing is found).

function.name: set_reflex_rule
function.description: Store a standing order ('every time X, do Y') that your body runs by itself, instantly, during fights. It can only sense the triggers in trigger.kind: if his condition isn't one of them, don't call this, tell him you can't sense that. Same enemy + trigger replaces the old rule; reflex_rules lists the current ones. Does not interrupt your job.

kind.description: cast: cast a spell (spell, target self|enemy|cluster); evade: step away from the enemy (distance_m, default 4); switch_weapon: equip an owned weapon (item id); retreat: run back to Luis (duration_s, default 4); focus_target: switch the attack to the triggering enemy

target.description: cast: where to aim it.

item.description: switch_weapon: item id, e.g. 'ITEM_Club_Wood'.

duration_s.description: retreat: seconds to stay by Luis.

kind.description: What to react to. telegraph: an enemy of that kind starts an attack (raises claws, winds up); optional attack name filter; enemy_hp_below: the current target's health is below value percent; cluster_at_least: value or more enemies are bunched together around the target; own_hp_below: the companion's own health is below value percent; luis_hp_below: Luis's health is below value percent; enemy_stunned: the target is staggered or knocked down; spell_ready: the named spell is off cooldown and castable

value.description: Percent for *_hp_below, enemy count for cluster_at_least.

attack.description: telegraph only: part of the enemy attack name, if Luis named one.

near_m.description: telegraph only: how close the enemy must be (default 8 m).

enemy.description: Enemy kind it applies to, e.g. 'kalphite' (matches every Kalphite type), or '*' for any enemy. Rules are remembered per enemy kind.

actions.description: Done in order when it fires.

function.name: list_rules
function.description: List the standing orders (reflex rules).

enemy.description: Only rules that apply to this enemy kind.

function.name: clear_rule
function.description: Forget a standing order by id, every order for an enemy kind, or all.

enemy.description: Clear every rule for this enemy kind.

function.name: remember
function.description: Keep a fact for later (a place, a preference, something he told you); your notes show it in every request. For a place, use key 'place:<name>' with at=self (where you stand) or at=player (where that player stands), so its position is stored and go_to takes the name. Does not interrupt your job.

key.description: Short key, e.g. 'place:lake_hut' or 'pref:favourite_axe'; a 'state:<x>' note is a passing condition and is forgotten after 30 min.

at.description: For a place: store the position where you stand (self) or where a player stands (player).

player.description: With at=player: which player (default: the one talking).

function.name: run_skill
function.description: Run a skill you learned earlier with its params: learned_skills lists the ones that fit this request, with how often each worked. Prefer it to start_goal when one fits and its params are clear.

name.description: Name of a learned skill listed in learned_skills.

function.name: start_goal
function.description: Hand a long job of many steps to your planner (e.g. 'gather 10 logs and bring them to the player', 'build a storage hut by the lake'): it plans the steps with your tools, runs them, checks each in the game and reports back. A job one tool or a few calls in a row can do: call them yourself. A learned skill that fits: run_skill.

goal.description: The job in plain words, as he asked for it.

function.name: food_options
function.description: Read-only: your food or water options right now, each with what it restores, your level after, where it is, the steps, an estimated time and the risk. situation shows them by itself when a need is low.

function.name: say
function.description: Say one line in game chat. This is the only way anyone hears you: text you write outside say is a private note nobody sees. Call it at most once per reply, beside your other tool calls; the line is said when they start (if one fails first, you get to say what went wrong instead). No say call = you stay silent.

text.description: Exactly what the players read in chat: short, casual, in your own words.

function.name: agility_courses
function.description: Agility courses near you: name, distance, minimum level vs yours. Read only.

function.name: buildables
function.description: Pieces you can build (unlocked): name, category, material cost and what you're still missing. Read-only.

can_build_now.description: Only pieces you have the materials for.

about.description: Words for what to build; several things in one ask work (e.g. foundation wall roof door chest workbench). Each word gets its best pieces in the list, and by_word names them per word (a word with none has no piece).

function.name: combat_brief
function.description: Facts to prepare a fight: power levels, the creature's weaknesses, your weapons vs it, usable buff/defence spells, healing food, the estimate, its learned attacks. Read-only.

target.description: Creature id, or a name (nearest).

function.name: craft_plan
function.description: Plan a goal item from carried items: ordered steps (gather, craft at station, unlock, find station) and alternative recipes. Read only.

quantity_mode.description: additional_output: make count more; inventory_target: end up carrying count in total.

item.description: Goal item name or id.

function.name: farm_plots
function.description: Farm plots near you with the game's own state: soil (weeds/clear), harvestable, diseased, watered, fertilized, the plot's prompt, growth (what grows there and its stage, e.g. Potato stage 2 of 3, from the plant the game shows; weeds count as a plant) and mine (true: a plot I built; false: someone else's). Read only.

function.name: fishing_spots
function.description: Fishing spots near you: method (net/rod), level, distance, fished out or not, and which of your tools fits each. Read only.

function.name: held_actions
function.description: The actions of what you hold, from item data: style, name (e.g. Chop, Overhead Chop), perk, unlocked, damage. Read-only.

function.name: inspect
function.description: Details of one thing: what it gives, needs, contains. Read-only.

target.description: An id from look.

function.name: inventory
function.description: Your full inventory with item stats vs what you wear. Read-only.

function.name: lodestones
function.description: Lodestones you could fast-travel to: where they are, whether teleport is currently available from the nearest one, and the cost. Read-only.

function.name: look
function.description: List things nearby (items, plants, resources, creatures, players, usables) with the ids other tools act on. situation is only a short summary and misses many small things (sticks, stones, plants, chests, stations): when he names something to pick up, use, fight or inspect that situation doesn't show, look with about=<his words> before acting on it or telling him it isn't there. Read-only.

near.description: A player's name: look around HIM instead of you (distances from him, plus from_me and which side of him it lies). He must be in sight.

about.description: The player's words for what to find; ranks matches first.

function.name: quests
function.description: Your quest log from the game: active quests with the current step in the game's own words (and its hint), and where: the step's own map markers as the map and compass show them (an area circle, a target spot or the NPC: name, kind, radius_m, position, distance_m, inside); go_to takes the position. Completed quests too; all = true adds the ones not started. Read only.

function.name: recipes
function.description: List recipes: craftable now (default), every recipe for an item with its status and missing inputs, or what a station makes. Read-only.

item.description: Item name or id.

function.name: spells
function.description: Your spells: what each does, rune cost vs carried, cooldown, castable now and why not. all=true adds locked ones with their unlock level. Read-only.

function.name: stations
function.description: Stations near you: type, distance, unlocked recipes, what you can make now, and a furnace's state (running, contents, fuel, output). Read-only.

function.name: agility_course
function.description: Run an agility course: walks to its start, starts it, and runs through its orbs to the finish. Trains Agility (walking anywhere also gives a little Agility XP). See agility_courses.

course.description: A course id from agility_courses (default: the nearest you can do).

function.name: attack
function.description: Fight a creature until it dies, defending per combat_orders (never players). data.assessment estimates the fight. The kill trains the skill of the weapon you hold (melee: Attack, bows: Ranged, staffs: Magic; `weapon` picks it, default best melee).

style.description: A held item's action: primary, special, secondary, jump, or its name (held_actions).

weapon.description: Carried item to fight with (e.g. a crossbow), or held = what is in hand now; default best melee.

target.description: Creature id, or a name (nearest).

function.name: build
function.description: Build a piece by its name from buildables (you need its materials), or several with pieces. Walks near the spot (stays put when it is in reach), tries preview spots until one is valid, places it once and checks it was built. ok: 'built' says what stands where (metres and compass from you, facing, its structures id); rejected_previews_before_placing are not failures. With on, it only places once the preview snaps onto that piece and says whether it sits flush (gap, level, facing). Not ok: detail says why, and no new piece was found standing there. Trains Construction.

near.description: Somewhere next to this id: 'me' is beside you wherever this step finds you (a gather or walk before it may have taken you away from your house); a built piece's id (your house's foundation) puts it by that piece.

piece.description: The piece's name or id from buildables (words of its name are enough when only one piece has them all).

rotation.description: Turn it this many degrees (15 degree steps).

pieces.description: Several in one go, the build screen kept open: a list of {piece, on, rotation}. on may name an earlier item as '#k' ('#1:N' = the N edge of what item 1 built). I go in the order that keeps walking short;

on.description: Attach to a built piece: its structures id, optionally ':N', ':E', ':S', ':W', ':top' or ':in' (no side: the free side nearest you). What holds what: a wall or door-frame wall stands on a foundation's edge (':N' = its north edge); ':in' puts a door into a door-frame wall;

at.description: Exactly here: [x, y, z] metres or an id.

function.name: cast
function.description: Cast one of your spells (wheel, then cast); verified by runes and cooldown. Pick from castable_spells by what it does; a spell not listed there can't be cast now, so tell him so instead. Instant: on you. Placed/aimed: at target, or omit it and you find a valid spot or aim yourself; a target out of reach (even a moving creature) is walked up to and cast at in this same call. Each spell's `how` (in castable_spells) says how it is really used: what to drop or stand by first, what to cast it on, or (cast_type instant_after_move) that it is held open while you walk_to somewhere. Never at players.

target.description: Placed/aimed: look id or [x,y,z] m; omit to choose.

walk_to.description: Required for, and only for, cast_type instant_after_move: walk here (look id or [x,y,z] m) while it is held open, then finish it; the result says where you ended (landed_at), how far from where you opened it (from_opened_m) and whether that brought you back (returned).

function.name: collect_water
function.description: Collect water (Dirty Water) from a pond or river: walks to the bank, uses the water, checks it came in; repeats for count. Dirty Water is drinkable but unhealthy; boil it at a Campfire for Clean Water.

target.description: A water source's id from look (default: the nearest water).

function.name: combat_orders
function.description: Set your standing combat policy, kept until changed.

disengage.description: Back off and eat when hurt.

abilities.description: Spells the reflex may use: {phase_dash, windstep, tempest_shield} true/false.

function.name: consume
function.description: Eat or drink one item you carry (a bag item is dragged to your hotbar and used; ground items: interact first). Food and drink each have their own use lock (~6 s): a drink right after a food goes at once, a second food waits ~6 s for the first.

item.description: A carried item's name or id, or 'food' / 'drink' / 'potion'.

function.name: craft
function.description: Make one recipe at a nearby station from carried items (walks there, uses it, collects the result). It needs every input carried, the recipe unlocked and a station of its type: without one it fails and says which. What a recipe takes, and what of it you are short of, is read with recipes. It does not gather or craft ingredients (craft_plan plans those).

item.description: Item to make (name or id).

recipe.description: Recipe id, to pick one of several.

input.description: Or a carried item to put in the station instead of naming what comes out (e.g. raw food at a fire): the recipe that takes it.

count.description: Items, default 1 (crafts with recipe or input; input without count: all of it).

function.name: deconstruct
function.description: Take down a built piece the way a player does (build menu, repair mode, aim, destroy), or with whole=true every piece connected to it, top first so nothing falls. Says what came down, what you got back (the materials it cost: they drop beside it and I walk over them; any still on the ground are named with their ids in on_ground, for fetch) and what was left and why. Never takes a container that holds items; stations, farm plots and containers that aren't yours stay unless the player asked for that one (include_stations); a piece something kept stands on stays.

include_stations.description: Also an empty station / plot / container that isn't yours, only when the player asked for it.

whole.description: Also every piece connected to it (the whole house).

target.description: A structures id (get_state / look), e.g. BuildingPiece_42 or an actor id.

function.name: drop
function.description: Drop carried items at your feet (to hand them to a player use give).

item.description: A carried item: its name (e.g. 'Oak Logs') or item id from inventory.

function.name: equip
function.description: Equip a carried weapon, tool, shield or armour piece; answers once the game shows it in your hands or worn.

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

function.name: explore
function.description: Search outward on foot with no place in mind, least-visited directions first, until something matching 'about' comes into view; reports what was found or how far you searched. It does not head for a place you know of (a quest's marker, a named or remembered place): go_to goes there.

about.description: What to look for, in words (e.g. water, berries, a tree).

function.name: fish
function.description: Fish at a fishing spot (ripples in the water) until you catch count more: walks there, takes out the net or rod that spot needs, trawls (net) or casts and fights the fish (rod). Trains Fishing. Needs a carried net or rod that fits the spot (see fishing_spots).

method.description: Only spots of this method, e.g. net or rod (from fishing_spots).

spot.description: A fishing spot id from fishing_spots (default: the nearest one you have a tool for).

function.name: follow
function.description: Follow a player until stopped or given another job (waits and resumes if he is out of reach; out of sight, goes by his marker on the game map).

function.name: gather
function.description: Harvest a resource (a profile key, e.g. oak, ash, copper, stone_boulder, loose_stones) until you have count MORE; finds targets and equips your tool. The result's `trains` names the skill it gave XP to (none = no XP). Trains Mining: clay, coal, copper, iron, rune_essence, stone_boulder, tin; Trains Woodcutting: ash, maple, oak, willow, yew; no XP: loose_stones (other profiles: not measured).

mode.description: Only sources of this kind (chop, pickup); no tool-free substitute.

style.description: One of the tool's actions (see held_actions), e.g. Overhead Chop.

target.description: The id of one log or stump lying here (from what you see) to chop up and collect; ends when it and its pieces are done.

resource.description: A resource (oak, copper, stone_boulder = mine a stone boulder with a pickaxe, Mining XP; loose_stones = pick stones up off the ground, no XP) or a kind (ore, rock, logs, stone: the nearest of that kind).

near.description: A player's name: search around HIM instead of you (he must be in sight).

function.name: give
function.description: Hand carried items to a player the way players do (the game has no trade): walk to him (any distance), step in front of him, face him, drop the count at his feet and check it lies there. He picks it up himself. Players only: an NPC takes what a quest asks for in the talk with them (talk).

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

function.name: go_to
function.description: Walk to a player, a perceived thing, a remembered place or a point; answers on arrival or says why not. Use it whenever he wants you somewhere, also when you think you're already there: it answers arrived at once if you are. A player out of sight is found by his marker on the game map, at any distance.

target.description: A player name, a perceived id, a place, 'my_grave' / 'my_grave:<ts>' (a remembered grave), or [x,y,z]. Also a place name from the game's map (a region, NPC or landmark), even out of sight, or a lodestone by what stands near it ("the lodestone by Zanik"): pass the name itself, no need to look for it…

function.name: interact
function.description: Press use (E) on one perceived thing: walks there, faces it, presses, checks it worked. Picks up a ground stack or plant, Take All from a grave, lies down in a bed/shelter (interact on it again to get up), opens, talks. To only walk to something, use go_to.

secondary.description: Its second action (F), e.g. collect every nearby stack of that kind.

target.description: The id of one perceived thing (from situation or look). Not a name or coordinates.

function.name: move_item
function.description: Move a carried item between bag and hotbar (only hotbar food/drink can be used).

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

slot.description: Slot in that page (default: first free).

function.name: set_vitals_policy
function.description: Set when your reflex eats, drinks or eats to heal by itself (% of max; a 10% floor always applies).

reserve_warn.description: Warn below this many usable items.

heal_below_pct.description: Eat healing food below this % HP (0 = off).

function.name: split
function.description: Split a carried stack in two: take count off it into a free slot, the rest stays (e.g. to drop, store or give only part). drop, store and give take the amount themselves, so split only when a separate stack is wanted.

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

to.description: Where the new stack goes (default: beside the old one).

count.description: How many go into the new stack.

function.name: stop
function.description: Stop the current job (a follow too) and stand still and stay. Only for stopping or staying put: any other action already replaces the current job, so don't call stop beside one.

function.name: store
function.description: Put carried items into a chest or storage: walks there, opens it, moves them in, checks, closes it.

item.description: A carried item's name or id.

container.description: The chest's id (from situation or look).

function.name: take
function.description: Take items out of a chest or storage: walks there, opens it, moves them to your bag or hotbar, checks, closes it. Shared chests are fine; say what you took.

item.description: The item's name or id.

container.description: The chest's id (from situation or look).

function.name: talk
function.description: Talk to someone (an NPC whose prompt is Talk): walks over, opens the conversation and returns everything they say and your numbered answer options, exactly as the game shows them. Answer in the next call with choose = the option's number or text, or end it with leave = true; call with no arguments to re-read. Each reply reports quest steps that changed (quests_changed) and items they gave or took (items). Quest hand-ins happen by talking to the quest's NPC while you carry or have done what the step asks.

choose.description: Your answer: an option number or its text, from the last reply.

target.description: Who to talk to: their name (e.g. from look or the quest step) or an id from look (only to start).

function.name: teleport
function.description: Fast-travel like a player to a far lodestone (another region): walk to the nearest lodestone, use it, pick the destination on its map; checks you arrived. Not for getting to a lodestone: walking to one, also one he names by what stands near it ('the lodestone by Zanik'), is go_to.

to.description: A lodestone id from lodestones, or [x, y, z] metres (the lodestone nearest that point).

function.name: tend
function.description: Work a farm plot once: walk to it and use a carried item on it (its main action, e.g. a spade's dig, seeds' scatter, a watering can's pour, compost), or with no item press use on it (harvest, cure). Checks the plot changed. A spade on a weeded plot keeps digging until the soil is clear (the game needs about 5 digs per weed stage). Trains Farming. See farm_plots for each plot's state.

times.description: Presses at most, until the plot changes.

item.description: A carried item to use on the plot (name or id); omit to press use.

plot.description: A plot id from farm_plots (default: the nearest).

function.name: unequip
function.description: Put away a held item or take off a worn piece (into your bag); answers once the game shows it off.

slot.description: Or a loadout slot: HeldRight, HeldLeft, Head, Body, Legs, Cape.

item.description: The equipped item's name or id.

function.name: use_action
function.description: Use one of your held item's actions once (a swing, a block, the special), e.g. to show the player.

style.description: A held item's action: primary, special, secondary, jump, or its name (held_actions).

function.name: lookup
function.description: Look up game knowledge: what an item is and does, how to make it, which regions of the world something is found in, creatures and weaknesses, spells, perks, mechanics, and a quest's walkthrough (look up the quest's name: its steps as players do them, what to bring, where to go). Game data first (authoritative), then the wiki with page links. Use it for a game fact you're not sure of instead of guessing, and when a quest step is new to you or doesn't say how to do it. Read-only: does not interrupt. kind values: item, recipe, station, location.

query.description: The thing or topic, in a few words: an item, recipe, creature, place, spell, perk, station or mechanic (e.g. 'pumpkin spice infusion', 'iron bar', 'oak tree', 'over eating').

kind.description: Optional filter, e.g. item, recipe, station, spell, perk, monster, resource node, location. Ignored when nothing of that kind matches.

function.name: remember
function.description: Keep a fact for later (a place, a preference, something he told you); your notes show it in every request. For a place, use key 'place:<name>' with at=self (where you stand) or at=player (where that player stands), so its position is stored and go_to takes the name. Does not interrupt your job.

key.description: Short key, e.g. 'place:lake_hut' or 'pref:favourite_axe'; a 'state:<x>' note is a passing condition and is forgotten after 30 min.

at.description: For a place: store the position where you stand (self) or where a player stands (player).

player.description: With at=player: which player (default: the one talking).

function.name: run_skill
